newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks surge on Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks surge on Greenspan comments.

text.p: Wall Street shares soared on Tuesday after the release of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's prepared remarks from his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress on the economy.
The Dow Jones Industrial average surged around 133 points, or 1.65 percent, to 8040, shortly after the text was released.
The long bond also roared higher, gaining over one full point to yield 6.46 percent.
The central bank chief said the Federal Reserve must be ready to act if needed to head off inflation but for now growth seemed to be slowing.

"I have no doubt that the current stance of policy...will need to be changed at some point," he said in the prepared tesimony to the House Banking subcomittee. "For the present, demand growth does appear to have moderated."
Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co, said Greenspan's remarks were not surprising.
"I think he was intent on not upsetting financial markets," Metz said. "Nothing he was said was...unsettling, which is really no surprise."
The Nasdaq composite rose 19 points, or 1.21 percent, to 1555.
